proposed.statement: Assign unit cost to every vertex of \(G_H\). Every vertex cover \(C\subseteq U\) maps to the intervention \(\{x_u:u\in C\}\) with the same cost, and every feasible intervention maps in polynomial time, by replacing each selected \(z_e\) with an endpoint of \(e\), to a vertex cover of no larger cost. Therefore \(\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H)\). The reduction is an \(L\)-reduction with constants one, so rank-three MCID is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hard even with unit costs and a radius-two bidirected tree; the \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness remains for source graphs of maximum degree three.
proposed.justification: Objective preservation identifies the exact complexity transition at the first nonempty rank rather than importing generic three-hitting-set hardness.
proposed.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove unrestricted MCID hardness, while Alimonti and Kann supply cubic vertex-cover hardness; neither gives a promise-preserving rank-three causal realization.
proposed.consumer: The two-carrier canonical reduction supplies structured hard instances for RC2 and Gurobi, with source and causal relabelings preserving the objective.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The guard-replacement reduction now depends explicitly on the independent source and causal encodings, their respective relabeling invariances, bit-cost accounting, and closure under composition; its graph and objective claim is unchanged.

proposed.statement: Given a supplied total order on \(V\), under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every nonempty \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size three and meets both \(P_s\) and \(T_s\). For an optimal \(y\) of the natural covering relaxation, every \(A_t\) is feasible for \(0<t<1/2\), and some breakpoint choice satisfies \(\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). Such a choice is found in polynomial time by the promised-rank enumerator using the supplied order.
proposed.justification: The parent-spouse crossing property improves the generic factor three for rank-three hitting set to the vertex-cover threshold two.
proposed.gap: Elahi and coauthors explicitly leave efficient MCID approximation as future work, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give only logarithmic approximation in general and exact polynomial algorithms through residual size two.
proposed.consumer: On the canonical causal encoding, and hence on a supplied finite causal carrier through \(V,\triangleleft_V\), the theorem gives a deterministic factor-two warm start.

proposed.statement: Given a supplied total order on \(V\) and a fixed promised rank bound \(r_0\), all inclusion-minimal residual hedges can be output exactly once, in the lexicographic order induced by the supplied order, in time \(|V|^{r_0+O(1)}\) and polynomial space. At \(r_0=3\) in the present bow-free singleton model, the runtime is \(O(|V|^3\operatorname{poly}(|V|))\). Given \(k\), branching on an uncovered residual returns the least-cost feasible intervention among sets of cardinality at most \(k\), or certifies that none exists, in \(O(3^k\operatorname{poly}(|V|,L))\), where \(L\) is the cost-encoding length.
proposed.justification: The proposition uses the supplied causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\), together with the rank promise, to provide exact-once lexicographic obstruction output while scoping exact weighted search to a supplied cardinality bound.
proposed.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash note polynomial subset enumeration at fixed hedge size, while Fernau assumes an explicit hyperedge list; neither supplies exact-once causal output together with the bounded-cardinality scope correction.
proposed.consumer: The canonical causal-vertex enumerator transfers only through \(V,\triangleleft_V\) and supplies a deterministic front end for the existing exact solver encodings.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Every enumeration, graph-search, rational-arithmetic, and bounded-branching runtime is now interpreted on the canonical causal encoding and transferred using the causal order only.

proposed.statement: Given a supplied total order on \(V\), enumerate all minimal residual hedges of size at most three in the induced lexicographic order, optimize or two-approximate that relaxation, and verify the returned \(A\) by alternating restriction of \(G[V\setminus A]\) to directed ancestors of \(s\) and the bidirected component of \(s\). If verification succeeds, an exact relaxation optimum is globally exact and the rounded answer costs at most \(2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). If verification fails, deletion-based minimization returns a verifiable \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) with \(|R|>3\).
proposed.justification: The interface safely exploits low rank without pretending to recognize the promise from a successful run.
proposed.gap: The WPMAX-SAT and ILP formulations of Elahi and coauthors solve unrestricted MCID but do not return a violated-rank certificate, while explicit bounded-rank hitting-set algorithms assume the promise externally.
proposed.consumer: On the canonical causal encoding, with transfer through \(V,\triangleleft_V\), RC2 and Gurobi users receive either a certified guarantee or a concrete large hedge.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Bounded enumeration, the polynomial rounding branch, fixed-point verification, deletion minimization, and their composition now depend explicitly on the causal encoding and never use the source carrier.

proposed.statement: The supremum of \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)/\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\) over all positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and \(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\) equals two. For every \(n\geq2\), the unit-cost private-guard expansion \(G_{K_n}\), formed using any total order, has a radius-two bidirected tree and ratio \(2-2/n\). Under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\), no polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists even on the narrower subclass of unit-cost instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\), nonempty residual clutter, and a radius-two bidirected tree.
proposed.justification: A matching gap family and conditional lower bound certify that factor two is the exact polynomial frontier under the standard conjecture.
proposed.gap: Khot and Regev establish the threshold for vertex cover, and Singh characterizes the source LP gap; no published result transfers the threshold to a bounded-rank causal-effect-identification design class.
proposed.consumer: Algorithm designers can treat factor two as worst-case optimal under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), with source and causal encodings kept distinct throughout the transfer.

prose_updates.tldr: Under the standard positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian semantics, acquiring \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\) identifies the causal target \(Q_s\) exactly when \(A\) hits every minimal residual hedge. Rank three is the first nonzero minimal residual-hedge rank for finite simple bow-free singleton-target ADMGs, and four-vertex hedges are exactly complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths. A one-private-guard expansion realizes every finite graph edge clutter and yields unit-cost \(\mathsf{NP}\)- and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness on radius-two bidirected trees. Under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), exact promised enumeration and parent-spouse thresholding give a weighted factor-two algorithm; complete-graph expansions show that the natural-LP gap supremum is two, and the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional \((2-\epsilon)\) lower bound transfers to the unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. Polynomial-time claims use two independent canonical encodings: \(V,\triangleleft_V\) for causal instances and \(U,\prec\) for source graphs, with polynomial binary rational arithmetic, composition, and carrier-specific relabeling transfer. The optimizer-or-rank-violation interface does not claim unrestricted rank recognition or unconstrained weighted \(3^k\) optimization.

project_justification.fill: The paper imports the positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian hedge-hitting identification bridge, then proves the four-vertex obstruction classification, exact private-guard realization, objective-preserving hardness, and the exact weighted natural-LP gap two at promised rank three. Source expansions use an order \(\prec\) on \(U\), whereas promised enumeration uses the distinct causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\). Correspondingly, a source graph is canonically encoded through \(U\simeq\mathrm{Fin}\,|U|\), while a causal instance is independently encoded through \(V\simeq\mathrm{Fin}\,|V|\); elementary graph and rational operations and guarded compositions have polynomial bit cost, and each result transfers only through the appropriate relabeling invariance. Complete-graph gadgets provide the matching gap sequence, the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional \((2-\epsilon)\) threshold holds on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass, and the bounded-cardinality and optimizer-or-violation interfaces retain their promised scope.

prose_updates.related_work: Richardson and Spirtes supply the finite simple ADMG and bow-free conventions. Shpitser and Pearl provide the complete hedge obstruction, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give its positive-compatible proxy-intervention formulation and the minimum-weight hedge-hitting program. They prove unrestricted hardness and polynomial solvability through residual size two; this paper establishes the first nonempty bow-free singleton boundary and its rank-three approximation frontier. Elahi and coauthors' RC2 and Gurobi formulations are direct computational consumers. Alimonti and Kann supply cubic Vertex Cover \(\mathsf{APX}\)-completeness, Khot and Regev supply the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional factor-two graph threshold, and Korte and Vygen supply rational linear programming in polynomial input time. Khot--Regev is adapted on the canonical source carrier \(U\simeq\mathrm{Fin}\,|U|\); rational LP and the causal algorithms are applied on canonically indexed inputs arising from \(V\simeq\mathrm{Fin}\,|V|\). Carrier-specific relabeling invariance, polynomial rational bit complexity, and closure under guarded composition transfer the results without conflating \(U,\prec\) with \(V,\triangleleft_V\). Singh's source LP-gap formula is only motivation for the independently proved complete-graph calculation, and Fernau's branching result informs only the scoped cardinality-bounded search. No unrestricted rank-three recognizer is claimed.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The factor-two algorithm is promise-based: polynomial enumeration is guaranteed only after \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and a causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\) are supplied, and a successful optimizer run does not certify the rank bound. The source order \(\prec\) on \(U\) is used only for private-guard construction and source canonicalization; it is not the causal enumeration order. Polynomial time is measured in carrier size and total binary input length \(L\) on the appropriate canonical encoding, with polynomially bounded rational intermediates, and transfer to a generic finite carrier requires its own supplied order and the corresponding relabeling invariance. The \(O(3^k)\) exact-search guarantee requires a supplied cardinality bound \(k\). Finite-sample allocation and statistical estimation remain outside this combinatorial identification-design result.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal bridge is imported under positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian semantics; no finite-sample or weaker-positivity extension is claimed. The exact weighted gap supremum covers positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and nonempty clutter, whereas the matching hardness subclass has unit costs and a radius-two bidirected tree. Every polynomial-time map is interpreted on its appropriate canonical binary representation: \(U\simeq\mathrm{Fin}\,|U|\) with source order \(\prec\) for source graphs, and independently \(V\simeq\mathrm{Fin}\,|V|\) with causal order \(\triangleleft_V\) for causal instances. Transfer to a generic carrier uses only the matching relabeling invariance; rational operations are charged at binary bit complexity and guarded compositions remain polynomial. Rank-at-most-three recognition, planar realizability, rank-four realizability, finite-sample allocation, and solver speedups remain open, and weighted \(O(3^k)\) search is asserted only with a supplied cardinality bound.
